Welcome to North London Grammar School
It is a privilege to be entrusted with a young person’s education. At North London Grammar School, we are dedicated to providing a safe, caring, and aspirational environment where every child can thrive both academically and personally. We create a nurturing space that supports growth, encourages ambition, and celebrates individuality.
Parents choose our school because we seek students who are motivated, curious, and committed to personal excellence. In return, we provide a setting where every child feels secure, inspired, and supported — enabling them to develop confidence, resilience, and a lifelong love of learning.
Our school is a joyful and successful community where pupils and staff alike are valued, respected, and empowered to achieve their full potential!

pageCache.text:

British Values
Five Rules of British Values
Introduction As How We Implement the British Values Into Education
As British Values are very important part of the education. The Department for Education states that there is a need:
“To create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”.
The Government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy defining British Values as follows:
Support for equality of opportunity for all
Tell Me More About North London Grammar School
North London Grammar School is a vibrant multi-cultural and multi faith school in the very diverse London Borough of Barnet. At North London Grammar School we take very seriously our responsibility to prepare children for life in modern Britain. All curriculum areas provide a vehicle for furthering understanding of these concepts and, in particular, our assemblies and lessons in Citizenship, RE and PSHE lessons provide excellent opportunities to deepen and develop understanding. Students embrace these concepts with enthusiasm and demonstrate a good understanding of their application to their own lives.
How Can My Child Adopt These British Values?
Our school reflects British values in all that we do. We aim to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British society and to the world. We encourage our children to be creative, unique, open-minded and independent individuals, respectful of themselves and of others in our school, our local community and the wider world.
How Can I Be Sure My Child Will Be Learning New Experiences?
The school makes considerable efforts to ensure children have exposure to a wide experience beyond their local community during which these concepts are shown, through, for example, a range of educational visits, visiting theatre groups, sporting events, our PGL residential trips, and through various visiting speakers.
Do The Parents Influence What Goes On In The School In Any Way?
Parents plan opportunities to voice their opinions through Parent Coffee Mornings and regular questionnaires. The outcomes of these forums act upon effectively, e.g. information evenings, homework policy, and the School Calendar. Students also involve in the planning of our creative curriculum, giving their thoughts on what they would like to learn. Our teachers weave these ideas into the curriculum. For instance, the ‘Child Net International’ for raising awareness of Internet Safety.
Democracy
As part of the British Values, Each year, students decide upon their class rules and the rights associated with these. All the students contribute to the drawing up of the class rules. We have a school council that meets at least twice a term. Elected School Council members involve in the meetings. The school council involve in gathering opinions about school issues such as environmental issues such as lighting and litter, charities to support, and other things like playtime resources. School council leaders emphasise on implementing a ‘majority rule’ when voting on particular issues.
The school makes considerable efforts to ensure children have exposure to a wide experience beyond their local community during which these concepts are shown, through, for example, a range of educational visits, visiting theatre groups, sporting events, our PGL residential trips, and through various visiting speakers.
The Rule of Laws And Discipline
North London Grammar School consistently reinforces the importance of laws, whether they are those that govern the class, the school, or the country, Pupils are taught from Year 7 the rules of the school. These are our School motto – Bonita’s, Scienta and Disciplina and the School Behaviour Ladder. We teach our pupils the value and reasons behind rules and laws and that they are there to govern and protect us. We also help our pupils to understand the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when people do not abide by the laws.
Visits from authorities such as the Police and Transport Police help reinforce this message. We, of course, reward modelling excellent behaviour. We also provide opportunities regularly for children and staff to participate in sporting activities which represent good examples of fairness, rules and etiquette in sport. Enrichment clubs (such as Karate, Table Tennis and Football) emphasize why rules and boundaries are necessary to ensure safety.
Individual Liberty
At North London Grammar School, we actively encourage the pupils to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we provide a structured and safe environment within which young pupils are able to make informed choices, whilst also receiving an empowering education. Pupils are given the freedom to make choices. They also become critical thinkers through evaluating, reflecting and collecting valid and reliable evidence. This makes good decisions, for example: whether it is through choice of challenge; how they record their learning using key skills to present information and communicate ideas; or by choosing to participate in our numerous enrichment clubs and opportunities.
Safeguarding our pupils is paramount and PSHCE/e-Safety lessons aim to equip pupils with the skills to make safe choices. We have provisionally planned a visit with The NSPCC on sessions on pupils’ right to be safe.
Mutual Respect
As NLGS, we revolved the Core Values such as ‘Goodness, Knowledge and Discipline’ around part of our school ethos and behaviour policy. Pupils take part in discussions and assemblies related to what this means. We also encourage the students to demonstrate responsibility for others at all times. NLGS centred our school reward system on our four school houses: Aeris, Aqua, Ignis, and Tellus. These involve all children from Year 7 to 12/13. We give rewards for positive attitudes and behaviours and there is a termly cup awarded to the House that has accrued the most House Points. The school goal and beliefs promote respect for others. This reflects our Behaviour Chart and reiterates through our classroom and school rules. High levels of mutual respect are obvious in school. They demonstrate daily the excellent relationships between staff and pupils.
Tolerance of Those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
North London Grammar School is an extremely diverse school. We actively promote diversity through our celebrations of different faiths and cultures. Religious Education, Citizenship and PSHE lessons reinforce messages of tolerance and respect for others. We encourage the members of different faiths and religions to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school. The children visit places of worship that are important to different faiths. We also welcome theatre groups who promote messages of equality and underline spiritual, moral, social and cultural values of groups of people around the world and within Britain. Therefore, we regularly audit resources in classrooms to ensure they reflect our multi-cultural society and stereotypes are challenged.

Welcome from the Headteacher
Inspiring A Love Of Learning
It is a true privilege to be entrusted with a young person’s education. At North London Grammar School, we are dedicated to fostering a safe, inspiring and inclusive environment where students feel known, valued, and inspired to reach their fullest potential.
Our mission is built upon our three pillars – Bonitas, Scientia and Disciplina. These are the core attributes we strive to instill in every student. We believe that every child possesses unique gifts, and our mission is to help them discover and develop these abilities, while also cultivating a deep-seated respect and understanding for others.
Parents choose our school because we seek students who are motivated to grow and behave positively in pursuit of excellence. In return, we offer a setting where students feel secure, inspired, and supported — enabling them to develop strong self-confidence, resilience, and a love of learning. Our school is a joyful and successful place where both pupils and staff are truly valued, respected, and empowered to succeed.
The success of our community stems from the high expectations from our dedicated teachers, staff and governors, paying close attention to each student’s progress, and the ongoing support of our families are at the heart of our success.
We warmly invite you to explore further and discover how we can journey together to nurture your child’s academic and personal story!

Behaviour Curriculum
Our Behaviour Culture
At North London Grammar School, we are committed to creating a calm, safe and supportive environment where all pupils can learn and thrive. Our approach to behaviour reflects our core belief that every child deserves the highest standards of care, learning and guidance, and that strong behaviour is taught, modelled and reinforced consistently. Our behaviour culture is rooted in respect, tolerance and trust, and supports our aim of developing confident, responsible and fulfilled young people who are a credit to themselves, their families and the school.
High Expectations, Clearly Taught
We have a clear Behaviour Curriculum which sets out the standards and routines expected of pupils in classrooms, corridors, social spaces and online. These expectations are explicitly taught through daily practice, assemblies, tutor time and staff modelling, so pupils understand how to behave positively and responsibly in all aspects of school life. Pupils are expected to be punctual, prepared for learning, courteous to others and committed to allowing everyone to learn without disruption.
Positive Recognition and Rewards
We strongly believe that positive behaviour should be recognised and celebrated. Pupils who consistently demonstrate excellent attitudes to learning, effort and conduct are rewarded through praise, merits, awards, leadership opportunities and celebration assemblies. These rewards reinforce our high expectations and encourage pupils to take pride in their behaviour and achievements.
Responding to Behaviour Concerns
When behaviour falls below the expected standard, staff respond calmly, fairly and consistently. Clear systems are in place to address behaviour, support reflection and prevent recurrence. Sanctions are proportionate and are always accompanied by guidance to help pupils learn from their mistakes and improve future behaviour. Where appropriate, restorative approaches are used to repair relationships and rebuild trust.
Support, Inclusion and Safeguarding
We recognise that behaviour can sometimes be linked to additional needs or wider concerns. Pupils are supported through pastoral care, SEND provision and safeguarding processes where necessary. Adjustments and additional guidance are provided to ensure our approach is inclusive and that all pupils are supported to meet expectations.
Working in Partnership with Parents and Carers
Strong behaviour is built through close partnership between school and home. We work collaboratively with parents and carers to support pupils’ behaviour, communicate concerns promptly and celebrate success.
How Behaviour Is Taught and Embedded
Behaviour at North London Grammar School is explicitly taught and consistently reinforced as part of daily school life. Leaders ensure that behaviour expectations are clearly defined, well understood and applied consistently across the school. Pupils are taught how to behave well through:
– A clearly structured Behaviour Curriculum outlining expectations in classrooms, corridors, social spaces and online – Explicit teaching of routines and standards, particularly at transition points – Regular reinforcement through assemblies, tutor time and PSHE – Staff modelling of respectful behaviour and positive relationships– Consistent application of rewards and sanctions so pupils understand the consequences of their choices
Staff are trained to create calm, purposeful learning environments, establish clear routines and use positive reinforcement to promote good behaviour. Where behaviour falls below expectations, responses are proportionate, fair and focused on improvement and restoration. Leaders monitor behaviour carefully to ensure expectations are upheld consistently and that pupils feel safe, supported and able to learn. Behaviour systems are reviewed regularly, and data is used to identify trends, ensure fairness and provide targeted support where needed. This approach enables pupils to develop self-discipline, respect for others and an understanding of how their behaviour contributes to a positive learning environment.
For full details of our expectations, rewards and sanctions, please refer to our Behaviour & Anti-Bullying Policy, available on this website

pageCache.pageTitle: North London Grammar School: Winner of the Independent Schools Association (ISA) Award 2025 - North London Grammar School
pageCache.text:
North London Grammar School: Winner of the Independent Schools Association (ISA) Award 2025
North London Grammar School has been recognised as the Winner of the Independent Schools Association (ISA) Award 2025 for International Provision voted for by a panel of expert judges, including school leaders and education experts, who look for standout stories of ambition, success, and achievement. The award celebrates the school’s flagship global initiative, the International Greenwich Olympiad (IGO).
In its fourth year, IGO has become a vibrant international platform, uniting over 500 students from 53 countries in project-based scientific and creative challenges. From the moment students raise their national flags together at the Opening Ceremony in Oxford to the sharing of traditional performances during Culture Night, the Olympiad celebrates diversity, intercultural understanding, and global collaboration. The event features an exhibition of scientific and non-scientific innovative projects, showcasing the creativity and talent of young people from around the world, followed by a celebratory Award Ceremony recognising their outstanding achievements.
The International Greenwich Olympiad collaborates with a wide range of global partners, including scientific networks, ministries of education, and affiliated organisations, highlighting its international reach and commitment to fostering innovation, intercultural exchange, and sustainability in education. Beyond competition, IGO serves as a transformative platform for intercultural networking, celebrating diversity, inclusion, and global collaboration, and inspiring young people worldwide to become creative, curious, and socially responsible changemakers.
“At North London Grammar School, we believe that education extends far beyond the classroom. The International Greenwich Olympiad reflects our commitment to nurturing curiosity, intercultural understanding, and leadership in our students. Receiving the ISA Award for International Provision is a proud moment for our entire school community, and we are deeply grateful to the team, students and partners who make this global initiative possible.” – Mr. Fatih Adak, Headteacher.

Before and After School Care
General Information
Before and After School Care provides activities for children Reception to Year 6, in a safe, happy environment, supervised by caring and experienced staff.
Before School Care
The Before School Care is open from 7:30am to 8:30am, and breakfast is provided. There is a choice of breakfast which includes cereals, toast, yoghurt, and fruit.
Please ensure your child is dropped off by 7.45am if you would like them to have breakfast.
The children will activities and play before starting school at 8.40 am.
After School Care
After-school care is open from 3:30 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. Each afternoon there is a planned play session led by one of our staff, and there are also plenty of games and themed activities to choose from. A quiet area is set aside where children can read, rest or do homework.
A light snack is provided on arrival. The menu includes a selection of freshly made sandwiches, cheese, crackers, and fruit. The choice of snack changes regularly.
Does my child have to stay for the whole session?
You can collect your child when it is convenient for you. However, if you have booked a full session and arrived early to pick up your child/ren, we cannot offer you a refund. The authorised adult must sign the attendee out from the club. After 5:00 p.m. = £15 late fee for each quarter-hour. If you have booked a place in advance and wish to cancel it, please give 24-hour notice, or you will be charged. Please contact via email to reception@northlondongrammar.com
Staff supervise children attending After School Care during club hours until they are collected by their parent/guardian (or an authorised adult). Children in Year 5 and under will not be permitted to go home unaccompanied, and children in Year 6 may do so only with the parent/guardian’s written permission. This written permission needs to clearly state the time the child may leave (and on which dates) parents/guardians are reminded that they have full responsibility for their child/ren from the time they are signed out of the club by a staff member.
Registration and Payment
Before your child can start, you will need to fill out a Registration Form, and there is a one-off registration charge of £5. Please book and pay for your sessions in advance. You can pay monthly or weekly to suit your needs. We accept internet payments made through the school payment system.
Once your family is registered with before / after school care, you can book emergency places at any time. These should be paid for on the day. Ask the school office to contact us. Alternatively, call 0208 205 0052 and speak to us during opening hours.
Activities and daily routines
The range of activities that the children can do at the club varies over the weeks. Here are just a few examples:
There is a planned activity led by one of our playworkers each day that the children can choose to participate in.
Art and Craft
Lego Club
Chinese Games & Culture
Table Tennis
Homework
Games and puzzles
Outdoor play/sports (dependent on weather)

Sibling discounts
A discount of 10% will be given on the above fees for bookings for second and subsequent children in the same family.
Users of both clubs
There will be a discount for people attending both Before School Care and After School Care.
Payment of Fees
Payment must be made in advance or on the day. Booking Forms are available from the Main Office and at the clubs.
Online: payments can be made via the school website.
Cheque: Payable to ‘North London Grammar School’. Please write your child’s name, class and which club the payment is for on the back of your cheque to ensure the correct allocation of monies.
Cash: Main Office. Money should be in a sealed envelope and clearly state your child’s name, class and which club the payment is for.
Please note: Should you require a change from your payment, please state this on the envelope.
Please remember:
Sickness, Accidents, First Aid and Emergencies
If a child becomes ill during a session, every attempt will be made to contact one of the people listed on the Registration Form to arrange the sick child’s collection. We will take care of the child until collection. In the case of a minor accident, basic First Aid will be administered. Medication can only be administered with specific written instructions from a parent/guardian.
In the case of an accident requiring more than basic First Aid, every attempt will be made to contact the parent/guardian to discuss the course of action to be taken. If a child needs emergency hospital treatment, the staff will first call an ambulance and then attempt to contact the parent/guardian and continue to do so until successful. A staff member will accompany the child to the hospital and remain with them until a parent/guardian arrives.
Please note: the Registration Form contains an Authorisation giving the Care Leader permission to act “in loco parentis,” e.g. the parent/guardian cannot be contacted in time, the Care Leader will invoke that authority to take action to gain appropriate medical treatment for the child.
Important Information
Before and After School care cannot accept any child to attend a session unless the parents complete and sign the Registration Form and submit it to the office.
Parents/guardians are responsible for ensuring that they always update the school with all contact details.
Safety and Security of Children
The safety and security of children attending our club are essential, and everyone concerned has a part to play. This policy has four features setting out everyone’s responsibilities involved with the club; parents, guardians, children, and staff.

pageCache.text:
North London Grammar School Celebrates Another Year of Outstanding GCSE Results
North London Grammar School (NLGS) is celebrating another strong set of GCSE results, with 53% of all GCSE grades awarded at grades 7–9 in 2026, rising from 51% in 2025. This marks the eighth consecutive year of improvement and sets a new benchmark for the school’s academic performance.
North London Grammar School GCSE Results 2026: At a Glance
These GCSE results reflect the strength of teaching and learning across North London Grammar School, as well as the sustained progress students make throughout their time at NLGS.
A Three-Year GCSE Programme Designed for Long-Term Success
A key feature of North London Grammar School’s approach to GCSE education is its three-year GCSE programme, which begins in Year 9. This gives students the time and space to develop a secure and lasting understanding of their subjects.
Rather than rushing through the GCSE syllabus, students progressively build their knowledge, revisit and consolidate key concepts, and develop the confidence, resilience and independence needed to perform at their best in their GCSE examinations.
The 2026 results demonstrate the benefits of this approach, with strong outcomes achieved across a wide range of academic subjects.
Strong GCSE Results Across Academic Departments
Students at North London Grammar School achieved particularly impressive results across several subject areas:
“We are incredibly proud of the achievements of our students in this year’s GCSE examinations. They have excelled across our creative, business and social science subjects, with particularly strong results in Art, Craft and Design, Business Studies and Psychology. These successes reflect the ambition, dedication and resilience of our students, alongside the expertise, commitment and high expectations of our teaching teams. It is wonderful to see our students’ hard work recognised in such a strong set of results, and we look forward to seeing them take these achievements into the next stage of their education.” – Mrs Erdil, Senior Deputy Head, Director of Teaching and Learning
A New Benchmark for GCSE Achievement
The 2026 GCSE results at North London Grammar School represent another significant milestone for the school and its students. With the proportion of grades 7–9 increasing for the eighth consecutive year, NLGS continues to build on its strong academic foundations.
For NLGS’s Year 11, Class of 2026, these results represent more than a set of grades. They reflect the progress students have made during their time at the school and the opportunities they have created for their next steps, with students progressing to leading colleges and a range of higher-education pathways.
With continued investment in teaching, learning and facilities, the school remains focused on providing students with the academic foundations. These results are a reflection of the hard work and commitment of students, alongside the dedication of teachers and the support of families. They also demonstrate the value of giving students sufficient time to develop deep subject knowledge and the skills required to succeed in their GCSEs.
Imran Class of 2026 (Year 11 student)
I am very happy with my results. l achieved eight grade 9s in Mathematics, English Language & Literature, all three sciences, Psychology and Geography. I’m now looking forward to studying A’ Levels at college and, ultimately, pursuing Dentistry at university. I’m grateful to my teachers at NLGS, whose commitment and encouragement prepared me well for these exams. My time at North London Grammar School has given me not only the academic foundation I needed, but also the confidence and support to pursue my next steps.
Roshni Class of 2026 (Year 11 student)
I achieved a total of nine grade 9s in Mathematics, English Literature, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Art & Design, Business Studies, Geography and Spanish. I joined NLGS in Year 9, and I feel it was one of the best decisions I’ve made. The fact that we started learning the GCSE curriculum a year earlier than most schools, I was able to learn the material without feeling too rushed. I feel that the head start really paid off, and I am thrilled to have finished my GCSEs this year with excellent results. I am deeply grateful to NLGS and all my teachers for their constant support and guidance in helping me achieve my best.

As a parent, I want to express my deepest gratitude to NLGS for the wonderful education and support provided to my child throughout her GCSEs. Starting the curriculum in Year 9 gave her a fantastic foundation and the confidence needed to excel, ultimately leading to her outstanding results this year. The school not only focuses on academics but also supports with extra-curricular activities such as Duke of Edinburgh and sports which helps them stand out for college applications.

My daughter has been at NLGS for five years and has done extremely well in her GCSEs. I am a very proud father. We are very pleased with the way her teachers have nurtured her and helped her to fulfil her potential. We chose NLGS because we felt she was not reaching her full potential at her previous school and would benefit from a more structured and academically focused environment. We are so pleased we made the decision to bring her to NLGS.

Mission Statement.
NLGS’s vision is of a community which provides an outstanding education for every individual attending it. Our mission in Learning support is to work together to reduce any barriers that prevent our children from becoming confident, high achieving and independent individuals. We are committed to ensure that NLGS will be a place of aspiration, where individuals, including all children with a special educational need and/or disability, matter and confidence flourishes so that achievement for all is outstanding.
Our guiding principle is one of Inclusion. Quality First Teaching remains our first response in relation to SEND issues, but we also ensure that the child receives high-quality additional support and interventions carefully matched to their needs where concerns are raised about a student’s level of progress despite the application of a variety of teaching strategies that have been put in place. We recognise that, in practice, individual children often have needs that cut across more than one area and that their needs may change over time. Our purpose is not to ‘label’ a child, but to work out what action the school needs to take. We consider the needs of the whole child and ensure that support is focused on individual need and personal outcomes rather than classification/label.
Types of Additional Support:
– Literacy Intervention– 1-1 support– Personalised/Individualised teaching based on need– Group support/study skills– Mentoring/Counselling– In-class Support– Use of laptop
Screening
All students are assessed for reading and spelling attainment on entry to NLGS. This gives us an initial indication of which students may need additional reading and spelling support. This may then be followed up with a subsequent, more diagnostic assessment. This gives us supplementary information about where the student’s specific needs lie. These results, plus KS2 SATS results and other information, are used by the SENCO (Special Educational Needs Coordinator) to identify students who may have learning difficulties. The decision to put a pupil on the SEND register is made as a result of consultation with as many teachers, professionals and parents as possible.
Review
The SEND register at NLGS is reviewed regularly. If progress is adequate, consideration will be given to removal from the SEND register. If progress is inadequate after several interventions have been put in place, we will consider extra interventions in consultation with parents and the pupil. Teachers and relevant professionals contribute to an IEP which is then collated by the SENDCo. If there are continuing concerns, NLGS can consider requesting a statutory assessment. This will be carried out by the Local Authority and an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) may be issued.
Parents
Our Learning Support department enjoys good working relationships with pupils and their families. We expect that relationship to start before a pupil joins the school. NLGS requires any SEND need to be shared and discussed with the school before a pupil is offered a place, so that we can determine the level of support that is required. The school cannot guarantee providing appropriate support for any special educational need that is not disclosed to the school before the offer of a place is made,
The department has an open-door policy where pupils and parents can raise any concerns. Pupils’ progress will be reported to parents through reports, and regular parents’ meetings and consultations. We also work collaboratively with external agencies, which help to guide and inform our support, when required.
Access Arrangements
At KS4 some students on the Learning Support Register are formally assessed by an external Specialist Teacher or Educational Psychologist in order to determine their eligibility for access arrangements for GCSE examinations. Students may need to be tested again in Year 12 to determine whether or not they still qualify for access arrangements for AS and A2 examinations.
The criteria for these arrangements are set out clearly in the Joint Council for Qualifications booklet which is published and updated every year. The school is subsequently inspected and required to present evidence in order to confirm our adherence to the regulations. These arrangements may include any or all of the following: up to 25% extra time, a reader, a scribe, the use of a laptop or rest breaks.
Access arrangements for Years 7-8 will be determined by our initial testing of students on entry to the school in Year 7 (please see Screening above). At this stage, however, access arrangements are put in place in a less formal capacity.
Despite access arrangements being put in place in key stage 3, there is no guarantee that this will lead on to access arrangements in key stage 4.

Key Stage 3 & 4 Curriculum Overview
Explore the comprehensive curriculum at North London Grammar School. Learn about subjects offered in Key Stages 3 and 4, GCSE pathways, and our commitment to academic excellence through international Olympiads.
Key Stage 3 (Years 7–8)
Students in KS3 follow a broad curriculum designed to build strong foundations for GCSE study. Subjects offered include:
Core Subjects: English, Mathematics, Science (Biology, Chemistry, Physics taught separately).
Humanities: Geography, History, Religious Education.
Languages & Arts: Spanish, Art, Drama, Music.
Technology & Wellbeing: Computer Science, Sport & PE, PSHE.
Students also participate in daily form time activities focused on Literacy, Numeracy, PSHE, and SMSC (Social, Moral, Spiritual, and Cultural development).
Key Stage 4 (Years 9–11)
In KS4, students follow personalised pathways aligned with their strengths and goals. All students study core GCSE subjects:
Compulsory GCSEs: English Language and Literature, Maths, Biology, Physics and Chemistry.

PSHE and Core PE remains a compulsory, non-assessed subject throughout KS4.

At North London Grammar School, we encourage academic excellence through participation in international Olympiads. With the support of dedicated teachers, our students have earned gold and silver medals—reflecting our commitment to nurturing talent beyond the classroom. What is IGO?
International Greenwich Olympiad (IGO) is a Project Olympiad organised and hosted by North London Grammar School in London, United Kingdom.
Our Vision
We strive to ignite a passion and enthusiasm in students for science and technology by tapping into their curiosity and creativity.
Our Mission
We offer an excellent platform that enables students to put their hands-on skills to good use, come up with new innovative ideas which they can convert to projects and present publicly in the form of research papers, display boards and other models.
Our Goals
– To assist students in learning more about and exploring scientific methods, techniques, and materials development while also obtaining new experiences through collaborative work with others.
– To encourage schools to work closely with their community and society. The parents of the participating students feel thrilled and proud watching their children designing their projects and being part of an international event. Parents also get a first-hand experience to get acquainted with various applications of science in their everyday life.
– To create a stimulating platform with indulging opportunities that offer a unique competition experience both on an individual and institutional level.
– To inspire potential future scientists, discover their talents and nurture them to become innovative inventors who will advance their society and humanity.
– To identify creative and talented students and provide them with exciting opportunities that will help further improve their skills.
– To help maximise students’ interest in science and, as a result, to make learning science an enjoyable experience for them.
– To encourage students to observe other students performing individually or in teams, so they can be inspired to pursue a future career in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics.
– To use science projects as an excellent tool to allow students to explore and experiment with different scientific theories and put them into practice.
– To provide opportunities to students and the wider community to be exposed to practical science applications in real-life situations.

Student Guidelines & Daily Procedures
Everything students and parents need to know about daily routines, lunch arrangements, personal items, and school safety — including break times, collection policies, and health procedures.
Break Time
Students need to be in supervised areas inside and outside the school buildings. We set specific rooms aside in the case of bad weather. Break time snacks are sold in the dining hall. Students must consume all food in the dining hall. We do not allow food consumption in other parts of the school, including outdoor areas.
Lunch Arrangements
Please inform the school of the intended arrangements for lunch. During lunchtime, entry into the dining hall is restricted to diners, and coats, bags, etc. should be left in the designated areas. We do not permit students into the classrooms during lunch.
Fees for school lunches are on the website. The parents can pay the fees to the finance manager or using the school account details. Please complete the payment at the start of each term.
Lunch Activities
Various clubs and societies hold meetings during the lunchtime break, and the library is open on designated days. Students will be given the relevant information by the staff involved. On very wet or cold days, students will remain indoors.
Personal Belongings
Please clearly mark School uniform, PE kit, school bags, etc. with your child’s name. Students should not bring expensive items to school.
We do not permit our students to use their mobile phones or any other smart devices in school. Bringing these to school will result in confiscation and parents will be requested to pick them up in person.
Please note that the school does not accept responsibility for any damage or loss to such items whilst in school.
Lockers
There are lockers available for all students within their classrooms.
Illness and accidents
If your child feels unwell or has an accident, they must tell a member of staff right away. Normally, they will be taken to the school office, where a trained First Aider will take care of them. If they are too ill to remain at school or if hospital treatment is necessary, we will contact the parents to make suitable arrangements.
Medicines
If your child needs to take medicine at school they must bring a letter stating when they need to take it. The medicine must be left with the Lead First Aider.

About NLGS
At NLGS, we take pride in knowing each and every one of our students. We put our students at the centre of all we do, and promote a clear set of values, which underpin the NLGS culture.
